results.content: From the examination of equations used to estimate the minimum effect size that could be detected with a specified level of statistical significance and power, it is shown that ignoring within-school clustering has clear methodolgical implications for the design of educational trials (class level clustering reduces statistical precision but this can be ofset through class level explanatory power). The differences between estimated and observed teacher-level clustering and covariate explanatory power led to reduced statistical sensitivity which is reflected on by the evaluators: "The discrepancy between the ICC at protocol and analysis stages is due to the prevalence of setting." (Worth et al., 2017 p27) Comparing the three primary and single secondary school 3-level CRTs, class level clustering seems to be stronger at secondary. So, whilst it is methodologically preferable to have a small samples of pupils spread across many classes, practicality suggests that it would be preferable to test all pupils in many classes - which has testing cost implications Perspective 2: Detecting an MDES of 0.20 sds The relationship between class level clustering and statistical power Assuming a 2-level two-armed balanced CRT design (or a 3-level design where 𝐼𝐶𝐶𝑐𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑠= 0.00), the sample sizes needed to detect an MDES of 0.20 standard deviations have been calculated using equation 2.0 (or 3.0) for different strengths of covariate explanatory power and school-level clustering. results.content: * ICC certification requires passing an exam for the chosen field, which typically takes a few hours and can be undertaken with either Computer-Based Training (CBT) or Proctored Remote Online Testing Option (PRONTO). * Preparation is important for passing an ICC certification test, for which the ICC website offers various resources; gaining prior on-the-job experience can be beneficial, and researching job opportunities that the certification affords you can aid in deciding which exam to take. Here are some examples of ICC certifications that are available: * CLA Swimming Pools: The Credential of Learning Achievement in Swimming pools is a certification that is bestowed on someone once they have successfully passed the required test. * F13 National Standard Residential Building Contractor: To pass the exam required to earn this certificate, test takers must demonstrate expertise on foundations, masonry, fire alarm systems as well as many other aspects of residential building safety. Many inspectors choose to take multiple ICC certification exams so that they are better equipped to handle any issues they face on the job.Related:8 Certifications for Construction Workers How to get ICC certification Becoming ICC certified in a particular field requires you to be at least 18 years old and pass a test designed for that specific certification. No work experience is necessary to take either test, but many inspectors choose to gain experience at a job before deciding to take the test.Related:Certificates, Certifications and Licenses: Differences and Jobs That Require Them Search jobs and companies hiring now Job title, keywords or company Tips for taking an ICC certification test Because ICC certification tests can take multiple hours and cost hundreds of dollars, it can be very beneficial to take time to prepare for them beforehand. Here are some tips for preparing to take an ICC certification test: ### Examine the materials on the ICC website The International Code Council's website is one of the best sources for finding study material for exams. Experiencing the material firsthand is often a good way to learn about the concepts that are covered on the test.Related:17 Certificates for Construction Professionals ### Explore the job opportunities that a certification gives you Before taking an exam, it can be helpful to research what jobs the exam qualifies you for.
